question: Can model-internal token confidence filter and stop parallel reasoning traces to improve accuracy and cut tokens relative to plain majority voting (self-consistency)?
hypothesis: Local confidence measures (group, bottom-10%, lowest group, tail) separate correct from incorrect traces better than a trace-wide average, so filtering low-confidence traces during or after generation raises accuracy and saves tokens.
contributions: DeepConf, a test-time method with offline mode (confidence-weighted voting with top-eta filtering) and online mode (early stop below a warmup-derived threshold plus consensus-based adaptive sampling)
Local confidence measures: group confidence, bottom-10% group confidence, lowest group confidence, tail confidence
Evaluation on five open models and five benchmarks with 64 repeated runs

method.summary: Token confidence is the negative mean log-probability of the top-k tokens. Traces are scored by local statistics, then (offline) the top eta percent vote with confidence weights, or (online) generation stops when the sliding-window confidence falls below a threshold taken from 16 warmup traces, and sampling ends once vote consensus reaches tau or the budget B is hit. No training; applied to existing open reasoning models.
method.task: Test-time scaling / self-consistency for competition math and GPQA-Diamond with extractable final answers

datasets.name: AIME24
datasets.source: Art of Problem Solving 2024 AIME I and II

datasets.name: AIME25
datasets.source: Art of Problem Solving 2025 AIME I and II

other.note: Table 1 and Table 2 use only DeepSeek-8B, Qwen3-32B, GPT-OSS-120B; appendices cover all five

inference.decoding: sampling; terminates on EOS or max length; answers parsed from \boxed{}
inference.samples: pool of 4,096 pre-generated traces per problem; each run resamples a working set of K (e.g. 512) from the pool; metrics averaged over 64 independent runs with fresh resampling
inference.prompting: Qwen3 and GPT-OSS: same instruction appended to every problem. GPT-OSS: provider's official system prompt, reasoning effort = high. DeepSeek-8B: official system prompt, problem in user message.

parameters.group window n: 2,048 tokens (512 and 1K also tested offline; text mentions n=1024 or 2048)
parameters.top-k for token confidence: top_logprobs=20 in the vLLM call (>=2 required); Table 11 top-k: 20 for Qwen3, 40 for GPT-OSS, none for DeepSeek-8B
parameters.stopping threshold s: Percentile(100-eta) of warmup trace confidences; Sec 4.1 also writes s = min over top-percentile warmup traces

metrics.name: Cons@K
metrics.definition: unweighted majority-vote accuracy with K traces

metrics.name: Measure@K / Measure+top-eta%@K
metrics.definition: confidence-weighted majority vote accuracy, optionally keeping the top eta% traces by confidence

metrics.name: Generated tokens
metrics.definition: total tokens over all traces; early-stopped traces count tokens produced before stopping

baselines: Self-consistency with unweighted majority voting (Wang et al., 2023)
Mean (average trace) confidence, self-certainty (Kang et al., 2025)
eval.protocol: 64 runs with fresh resampling from the 4,096-trace pool; no significance test stated; no seeds stated

availability.code: project page jiaweizzhao.github.io/deepconf; vLLM edits listed in Appendix G

limits: Needs token log-probabilities (top_logprobs>=2) and a patched vLLM; hosted APIs that hide logprobs cannot run it.
Only open-weight models; four of five benchmarks are competition math and GPQA-Diamond is the only other; tasks need a checkable boxed answer.
Authors concede overconfident wrong traces: 'addressing cases where models exhibit high confidence on incorrect reasoning paths, which is a key limitation observed in our experiments.'
Top-10% filter hurt 8 of 20 settings; Qwen3-8B AIME25 and several GPT-OSS cells lose accuracy online.
Results are averaged from resamples of a fixed 4,096-trace pool, not fresh generations; no hardware or wall-clock reported.
Abstract claims no hyperparameter tuning but eta, tau, Ninit and window size are set choices; warmup needs 16 full traces per problem.
The paper tests only one prompt sentence; it does not test whether it matters.
Abstract numbers 99.9% (offline) and 84.7% (online) come from different configurations.
